newsitem.title: USA: August construction spending rebounds from July drop.
newsitem.headline: August construction spending rebounds from July drop.

text.p: Spending on new construction rebounded in August from a July drop, the Commerce Department said Wednesday, largely because of a jump in privately financed business building.

Total construction was up 0.9 percent to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of $562.1 billion in August after falling a revised 1.1 percent in July. Previously, the department said July spending was down more sharply, by 1.4 percent.
All the gain in August construction spending occurred in the private sector, where outlays increased 1.3 percent to a rate of $423.4 billion following a 1.2 percent decline in July.
By contrast, public, or taxpayer-financed, building projects posted a 0.2 percent spending decrease in August after declines of 0.7 percent in July and 0.3 percent in June.

Private spending on non-residential building construction climbed strongly, by 3 percent in August to a record rate of $139.5 billion after a 1.6 percent drop in July. Spending increased to build new hotels, schools, hospitals and commercial buildings.

On the public construction side, there was reduced spending in August for new highways and streets, conservation projects and military projects, but a pickup in outlays for sewers, schools and water supply plants.
After allowing for inflation, total construction spending was up 0.7 percent in August to a seasonally adjusted $488.1-billion annual rate after a 1.6 percent fall in July, the department said.
